title: The Bridge That Was Coming Undone
story: High between two cloud-spires, a bridge of woven vapor holds 47 fledgling wind-finches who are too young to fly. Vuldreth the Mist Unraveler is tugging the bridge apart thread by thread, and the weather-wardens say it will hold for exactly 22 more minutes. Mr 6 straps on a rescue basket that carries at most 6 fledglings at a time, and each trip across and back takes 2.5 minutes.
question: If Mr 6 ferries every fledgling to safety using full baskets whenever he can, how many minutes will be left before the bridge unravels?
solution: 47 fledglings in baskets of 6 means 47 ÷ 6 = 7 remainder 5, so Mr 6 needs 8 trips (that last small basket still counts).
22 - 20 = 2 minutes left before the bridge unravels.
praise: Dividing 47 by 6 was exactly the right opening move — the leftover 5 fledglings still need a whole trip of their own, and that extra trip changes the clock.
hint: First ask: how many basket-loads does it take when 6 fit at a time and 47 are waiting? Leftovers still need a full trip.
victory: With two whole minutes to spare, Mr 6 tipped his helmet as the last thread sighed loose — and Vuldreth, finding nothing left to unravel but empty mist, wandered off to bother a cloud instead.
imagePrompt: A brave number-six knight with a blue cape carrying a basket of tiny fledglings across a fraying bridge of glowing vapor between two sky-spires, while a long wispy mist-creature tugs threads loose in the golden dawn light.
